title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 6 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Measurement: Surface Area and Volume

questions.prompt: Calculate the volume of a cylinder with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm, correct to one decimal place.
Calculate the surface area of a sphere with radius 3 cm, correct to two decimal places.
A cone has radius 3 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. Calculate its volume, correct to two decimal places.
A cone has radius 5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. Find its slant height.
Find the volume of a square-based pyramid with base 6 m and perpendicular height 10 m.
If all dimensions of a box are tripled, its surface area is multiplied by…
Halving the radius of a sphere makes its volume one-eighth of the original.
Find the total surface area of a closed cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm, correct to one decimal place.
The angle at the circumference subtended by an arc is $38^\circ$. Find the angle at the centre subtended by the same arc.
AB is a diameter and C is on the circle. What is the size of $\hat{ACB}$?
In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, $\hat{A} = 105^\circ$. Find $\hat{C}$.
The angle between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact is…
Angles subtended by the same chord in the same segment are equal.
A circle has radius 13 cm. A chord is 5 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
Match each statement to its reason.

pairs.left: PA = PB for tangents from P
Angle between tangent and chord equals angle in alternate segment
Exterior angle equals interior opposite angle
OM bisects chord AB when OM ⊥ AB

questions.prompt: TA is a tangent to the circle at A. Chord AB makes $\hat{TAB} = 70^\circ$, and C is a point on the circle in the alternate segment. Find $\hat{ACB}$, and $\hat{AOB}$ if O is the centre. Give reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ $\hat{ACB} = 70^\circ$ (tan chord theorem) (2)
✓ $\hat{AOB} = 140^\circ$ (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circumference) (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Trigonometry: Sine, Cosine and Area Rules

questions.prompt: You know all three sides of a triangle and want an angle. Which rule should you use?
In △ABC, $\hat{A} = 30^\circ$, $\hat{B} = 45^\circ$, $a = 10$. Find $b$, correct to two decimal places.
In △ABC, $b = 5$, $c = 7$ and $\hat{A} = 60^\circ$. Find $a$, correct to two decimal places.
When using the sine rule to find an angle, there may be two possible triangles.
In any triangle, the largest angle is opposite…
A triangular field has sides 80 m and 120 m with an included angle of $65^\circ$. Find the length of the third side and the area of the field.
Two ships leave a harbour at the same time. One sails 30 km on a bearing of $040^\circ$ and the other 45 km on a bearing of $110^\circ$. How far apart are they?
A laptop costing R12 000 depreciates by 20% p.a. on the straight-line method. What is it worth after 3 years?
A tractor costing R400 000 depreciates at 12% p.a. on the reducing-balance method. Find its value after 6 years, to the nearest rand.
Convert 12% p.a. compounded quarterly to an effective annual rate, as a percentage correct to two decimal places.
For an investment over 4 years with interest compounded monthly, what is $n$?
R5 000 is invested at 7% p.a. compounded monthly for 3 years. Find the final amount, correct to the nearest cent.
For the same nominal rate, interest compounded monthly gives more than interest compounded annually.
R20 000 is invested at 9% p.a. compounded annually. After 3 years, R5 000 is withdrawn. What is the balance after 5 years?
An effective rate of 10% p.a. is required. What nominal rate, compounded monthly, gives this?
A and B are mutually exclusive with $P(A) = 0{,}3$ and $P(B) = 0{,}45$. Find $P(A \text{ or } B)$.
Which situation involves dependent events?
The probability that a bus is late is 0,2 each day, independently. Find the probability that over two days the bus is (a) late on both days (b) late on exactly one day.
A box has 4 green and 6 yellow balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Find $P(\text{both green})$.
Of 150 people, 90 own a car. Of the car owners, 54 are employed full-time; 60 of the 150 are employed full-time. Is owning a car independent of full-time employment? Show working.
questions.memo:
✓ $P(\text{car}) \times P(\text{employed}) = 0{,}6 \times 0{,}4 = 0{,}24$ (1)
✓ $P(\text{car and employed}) = \frac{54}{150} = 0{,}36$ (1)
✓ Not equal, so the events are dependent (1)
